extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on assessing amendments to patent specifications and claims under the Korean Patent Act (esp. prohibitions on addition of new matter, Article 47(2)/(3); refusal-to-enter rules under Articles 51/63). Directed at examination/evaluation of claim/specification amendments and procedural handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters described in the specification or drawing(s) as originally filed; matters that a person skilled in the art would clearly recognize from the disclosure of the specification or drawing(s) as originally filed shall be deemed to be included in the scope of the disclosure of the original specification or drawing(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both explicit text/figures and what a skilled person would clearly recognize from those originals when determining whether an amendment adds new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority / prior-filed application not basis for new-matter assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Since a first country application or a prior-filed application which forms the basis of the priority claim shall not correspond to the specification or drawing(s) as originally filed, such applications shall not be used as the basis of assessment in addition of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on priority or earlier-filed documents as supplying original disclosure support when assessing whether an amendment introduces new matter into the current application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract excluded from original-disclosure assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Since an abstract shall not correspond to a specification or drawing(s), an abstract shall not be included in the specification or drawing(s) which forms the basis of assessment in addition of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat content appearing only in an abstract as supporting the specification for amendment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing an incomplete invention viewed as adding new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of completing an incomplete invention, the amendment shall be deemed to add new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that attempt to 'complete' an invention that was incomplete in the original disclosure are generally treated as introducing new subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing from genus to species requires original support or skilled-person recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment is made to narrow a claim as from a genus to a species, unless the species is supported by the original specification and drawings, or unless one skilled in the art would readily recognize the species from the genus in light of ordinary skill in the art at the time the patent application was filed, it shall be viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: inserting a specific material (e.g., 'ABS') into a previously generic 'transparent plastic' may introduce new matter unless ABS was disclosed or would be obvious to skilled person. Conversely, if the skilled person would intuitively associate the generic term with the specific embodiment (e.g., 'sensor detecting rotation' -> 'proximity sensor'), amendment may be supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening from species to genus and deletion of essential limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment is made to broaden a claim as from a species to a genus, if the genus encompasses other species than the species disclosed in the original specification, and if the other species may have different function in addressing the problem to be solved or may accomplish different effects, the amendment shall constitute introduction of new matter. Where some limitations are deleted and the deleted limitations are described in the original disclosure as essential in solving a problem, it shall be viewed as introduction of new matter. However, deleting arbitrarily added limitations having nothing to do with solving problems may be supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether broadened claim covers embodiments with different effects/functions and whether deleted features were essential; examples include geometry changes affecting electrical contact, or deletion of an 'identifying code' limitation that was arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical-range amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment is made for adding or changing or narrowing numerical range, unless new numerical range is disclosed in the original specification and unless it can be derived from the description of the original specification, it shall be viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation may be acceptable when ranges are logically deducible from original disclosures (example: deducing melting point limits from disclosed melting and process temperatures), but arbitrary or novel numeric ranges are new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative limitations (deleting elements) permitted only if no new technical matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment to delete some elements from the claims ('negative limitations') is permitted; provided, however, that such a negative limitation does not introduce any new technical matter which is not disclosed in the original specification. In particular, excluding particular subjects (e.g., humans) is acceptable if original specification did not restrict to particular animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: amending 'treatment methods for mammals' to 'except humans' may be permitted where original disclosure did not limit to humans. Ensure deletion does not implicitly introduce an unsupported technical teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining separately disclosed embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where separate configurations or embodiments independently described in the original specification are combined as a single invention by an amendment, unless such a combination is described in the original specification or unless one skilled in the art can easily derive the combination taking into consideration common technical knowledge at the time of filing, it shall be viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: combining features from two separately disclosed refrigerator embodiments (shaking lever + conveying unit) can be new matter if original did not describe them together or make their combination obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding embodiments or test examples generally adds new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment to add an embodiment or a test example shall be generally viewed as introduction of new matter; provided, however, that where the amendment is deemed to fall within the scope of the disclosure of the original specification, it shall not be viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding entirely new exemplifying embodiments or test data is usually impermissible unless the added content is clearly within what the original disclosure already enabled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding new effects generally adds new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment to add new effects of the claimed invention shall be generally viewed as introduction of new matter; provided, however, that where one skilled in the art could easily recognize the effects from the configuration of the invention disclosed in the original specification or where it is commonly known in the relevant field that such effects can be accomplished from the configuration described in the original specification, it shall not be generally viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious when adding statements of advantages/effects; allowed only if those effects are directly and unambiguously derivable from the original configuration or common general knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding titles/summaries of prior art vs. adding prior-art disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment to simply add the title of prior art documents and the amendment to add both the short summaries of the prior art documents and the title of the documents shall not be viewed as introduction of new matter. However, where the disclosure of a prior art document is added to address lack of written description or to complete an incomplete invention, or where comparisons suggesting advantages are added, it shall be generally viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted: inserting citation titles or brief summaries. Not permitted: inserting the substantive disclosure of prior art to fill original-specification gaps or to assert advantages of the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding well-known prior art may be new matter if not implicitly described
rubrics_metrics.description: Though the added matters through amendment are well-known prior arts, if a person skilled in the art does not clearly recognize the added matters as implicitly described in the original specification or drawing(s), the amendment of adding such well-known prior arts shall be deemed as addition of new matter out of the scope of the disclosure of the specification or drawing(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume that 'well-known' status alone justifies adding content—there must be clear implicit disclosure in the original filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of obvious errors permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where one skilled in the art would not only recognize the existence of the error in the specification but also recognize the appropriate correction, an amendment to correct an obvious error does not constitute introduction of new matter. Further, where one skilled in the art clearly understands which of two or more conflicting descriptions is correct based on the disclosure of the original specification or drawing(s), the amendment of correcting the conflicting descriptions shall not be deemed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obvious typographical or unambiguous errors may be corrected without constituting new matter; require that skilled person can clearly identify the correct text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reply to rejection or on request for reexamination must satisfy Article 47(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment in reply to the rejection necessitated by a previous amendment or carried out upon a request for reexamination shall additionally satisfy Article 47(3), along with Article 47(2) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When responding to a rejection arising from an earlier amendment or during reexamination, ensure the amendment both avoids new matter (47(2)) and meets the procedural/content limits for permissible amendments under 47(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible amendments under Article 47(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to claims among the amendments in response to the rejection necessitated by a previous amendment or upon a request for reexamination in accordance with Article 47(3) of the Patent Act shall be one of the followings: narrowing of claims by restricting claims, correction of clerical errors, clarification of ambiguous descriptions, or deletion of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only these types of amendments are allowable under Article 47(3) when replying to such rejections; assess amended claims against the earlier (same-numbered) claim to determine correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of claim restriction (narrowing) permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases of narrowing of claims under Article 47(3) shall be limited to restricting a claim, deleting a claim and adding a technical element to a claim. Restricting includes reduction of numerical range, change from genus to species, deletion of alternatively recited elements, and reduction of referred claim from claims which refer to multiple claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction of a numeric range is permitted only if it stays within the original claim's range; simultaneous reduction and extension (e.g., 10-20→15-30) is not reduction. Deleting alternative elements (A or B → A) is a valid restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion of a claim is a legitimate amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Deletion of a claim shall be recognized as a legitimate amendment since it constitutes restriction of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deleting claims is allowed; adjust citations and dependent claims accordingly (changing citation numbers or adding cited contents may be treated as correcting incorrect description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding described technical features to narrow claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of an invention is narrowed by adding new technical features described in the description of the invention or claims (e.g., changing 'B attached to A' to 'B attached to A and then C attached to B').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding features that are already described in the description/claims narrows and is permissible as a restriction, provided support exists in the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not falling under Article 47(3)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases not falling under Article 47(3)(i) include: (i) where a claim is newly-added or an invention is added to claims by adding alternative elements or adding a referred claim (with some reorganization exceptions), and (ii) where a claim goes beyond the original scope due to certain amendments (change from species to genus, deletion of elements, addition & deletion of elements, broadening numerical range, replacement of element, change of numerical range).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to newly added matter or amendments that broaden scope—these are not permitted under Article 47(3) and may be refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of clerical errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Correcting clerical errors refers to the case where a description before an amendment and a description after an amendment are objectively deemed to be the same. Examples include incorrect description of claims explicitly recognized from matters in the description or where incorrectness is explicit based on features or empirical rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only true objective/correctable clerical mistakes qualify; ambiguous edits that change substantive meaning are not clerical corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of ambiguous descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An ambiguous description is one whose meaning in the context is not clear (e.g., unclear claim language, elements that do not match other descriptions, or the claim is not technically specified). An amendment of redrafting the overall claim without any substantial changes shall be deemed to clarify an ambiguous description under Article 47(3)(iii), unless other specific conditions are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redrafting for clarity is allowable provided no substantive change to scope; determine whether the redraft merely clarifies or actually changes the technical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments deleting previously added new matter (reinstatement/deletion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new matters are added at a particular stage of amendment, an amendment for reinstating the original claim before addition of new matter shall be permitted. In addition, an amendment of amending claims according to Article 47(3)(i) to (iii) while deleting the new matter shall be permitted. An examiner shall assess legitimacy by comparing claims before addition of new matter with amended claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstating or deleting earlier-added new matter is allowed to cure prior improper additions; examiners must compare pre-addition claims with current amendments. Examples given illustrate permitted and refused sequences (e.g., reinstatement permitted; deleting a claim with new matter permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter amendments (Article 51) when violating Article 47(2)/(3) or causing new rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner finds that an amendment made under Article 47(1)(ii) or (iii) violates paragraph (2) or (3) of the same Article, or that another ground of rejection necessitated by the amendment arises (excluding an amendment to delete a claim among certain amendments), he/she shall refuse to enter the amendment with a decision, except in specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions to refuse must be in writing stating grounds; generally no appeal permitted against refusal to enter amendment (with limited exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and assessment of 'new rejection necessitated by amendment'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new rejection necessitated by the amendment' means a ground for rejection which did not exist prior to the amendment newly arises due to the submission of the amendment (e.g., amendment renders claim indefinite or creates new lack-of-novelty or lack-of-inventive-step grounds). Rejection grounds that were present before the amendment but not notified are not deemed new grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing refusal, determine whether the amendment itself created the new ground; pre-existing but unnotified grounds are not treated as 'new'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination method for refusal to enter amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an amendment made after the final rejection necessitated by a previous amendment or an amendment upon a request for reexamination meets the requirements shall be assessed regardless of an order of amendment requirements. If multiple requirements are not satisfied, an examiner shall point out as many unsatisfied requirements as possible and refuse to enter the concerned amendment. If any amended matter violates Article 47(2)/(3) or (except for deletion) necessitates a new rejection, the whole amendment shall be refused to be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess all amended matters individually; use the amendment forms to identify units of amendment; when multiple amendments submitted during the reply period, assess per amendment; for filings on/after July 1, 2013 treat last amendment as effective where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautions and procedural rules regarding refusal and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural cautions include: when multiple amended matters are submitted assess each matter one-by-one; amendments submitted on the same date are assessed per amendment; if a decision to reject has been revoked and the case remanded, prior revocation findings bind the examiner; if refusal to enter is later revoked on appeal, examiner may still refuse on new grounds not reviewed on appeal in certain limited contexts; rules protect applicants from harsh results when appeals are pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedural safeguards (reexamination of pre-amendment specification when refusing amendments, remand binding findings, special handling when appeals exist) and document reasons in writing as required by Article 51/63.
